Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of needs (from our conversation):
- Primary workload: real-time customer support assistant with mixed short/long prompts (avg. seq len ~ 512 tokens, spikes to 2k for context)
- SLA target: 200ms p50 for critical flows, best-effort for bulk batch jobs
- Data controls: must stay within VPC for PII-sensitive routes; some non-sensitive flows can use hosted API
- Expected steady-state qps: 15-20 r/s with occasional bursts to 60 r/s during peak events

Candidate deployment modes we discussed:
1) Hosted API for non-sensitive, low-latency features (per-token billing)
2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable throughput and lower unit cost on steady traffic (monthly/annual commit)
3) Private (VPC) deployment for PII-sensitive flows or full on-prem for regulated workloads (license + infra)

Requested follow-ups from you:
- Confirmation on which routes must be private vs can go hosted
- Approximate monthly tokens and % of traffic that will be PII-sensitive (to model split economics)
- Any procurement timeline / required security artifacts (SOC2, IPAR)

Action items from our side: 
- Marissa will put together a cost model comparing per-token hosted pricing vs commit-based Dedicated pricing and a sample Private deployment cost (infra + license).
- I'll share a short comparison doc and HubSpot deal link.

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up on Wednesday (11/24) to review the cost model and decide preferred deployment split. Does that time work?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / team —

Attached is a first-pass cost model (acmeai_cost_model_v2.xlsx) and a short PDF summary (redwood_dedicated_pricing_sheet.pdf). High-level notes below; we'll walk through numbers in the Wed 11/24 call at 10am PT as agreed.

High-level: recommended split for cost + SLA balance
- Private (VPC) for PII-sensitive routes (~30% traffic): assumes single-region VPC deployment (customer-managed infra). One-time license & onboarding + monthly support fee. Estimated infra ops + infra amortized: $18k/month (baseline) + license $25k one-time.
- Redwood Dedicated for steady-state core API traffic (~50% traffic): 3x reserved GPU nodes (NVIDIA H100 class equivalent) with burst capacity. Monthly commit pricing modeled; effective per-token cost drops ~40% vs hosted when commit utilization >70%.
- Hosted API for burst and non-critical enrichment (~20% traffic): per-token pricing; best for irregular spiky traffic and avoids infra ops.

Key assumptions (see sheet tabs):
- Avg seq length 512 tokens (weighted), 1.2B tokens/month baseline
- Dedicated commit modeled at 3x A100/H100 tier with monthly commit term; calculates amortized cost per token at 70% and 90% utilization scenarios
- Hosted per-token: list price used for baseline; negotiable with volume tiers

Preliminary numbers (rounded):
- All-hosted (baseline): ~$0.12/token effective (for our pricing bands) -> monthly ~$144k (1.2B tokens)
- Blended (Private 30% + Dedicated 50% + Hosted 20%): ~$0.073/token effective blended -> monthly ~$87.6k (includes infra amortization + license)
- Costs are sensitive to utilization: moving Dedicated utilization from 70% -> 90% reduces blended monthly by ~12%

Next steps / asks for accuracy:
1) Confirm token split (30/50/20) or provide expected split per route
2) Share any existing dedicated capacity/commit commitments for vendor comparisons
3) Procurement timeline and PO cadence so we can model commit start dates and potential onboarding windows

I'll present the sheet and the assumptions on Wed 11/24 10:00am PT. If you want any alternate scenarios (single-region vs multi-region Dedicated, or smaller commit footprints), tell me and I'll add a tab.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
